rationale: The pain is real and recurring — shared-hosting outages affect freelancers and small businesses financially — but the evidence base is a single low-score HN post (4 points), and the market for uptime monitoring is saturated by well-funded incumbents (UptimeRobot free tier, Better Uptime, StatusCake) with no clear differentiated moat. The willingness-to-pay signal is entirely implicit (existing hosting spend), and there is no documented instance of users actively paying for a failover add-on over and above free-tier monitors. Fails the 5-distinct-pain-quotes threshold and the explicit WTP requirement.
